questions.question: Identify and Examine the purpose of an interface in Java.
questions.solution_html:
• An interface in Java is used to define a contract that classes must implement. An interface in
  • Java is a collection of abstract methods and constants. Purpose: Achieves abstraction (only
  • method declarations, no implementation), Supports multiple inheritance.
  • Multiple Inheritance (through interfaces only)
  • interface A {}
  • interface B {}
  • class C implements A, B {}
  • Java does not support multiple inheritance using classes. It is achieved using interfaces.

questions.question: What are labelled loops in Java? Explain their purpose with syntax.
questions.solution_html:
• A labelled loop in Java is a loop that is assigned a name (label). It is mainly used with break and
  • continue statements to control the flow of nested loops. Purpose: Helps to exit or continue an
  • outer loop from within an inner loop. Improves control in complex nested loop structures. Give
  • an example.

questions.question: Use the Delegation Event Model to explain how events are handled in Java.
questions.solution_html:
• Use the Delegation Event Model to explain how events are handled in Java.
  • Java uses the Delegation Event Model for handling events in GUI applications.
  • Components: Event Source – Component that generates the event (e.g., button)
  • Event Object – Contains information about the event. Event Listener – Handles the event
  • Working: A source generates an event. The event is passed to a registered listener. The listener
  • processes the event using handler methods. Give an Example
  • High Performance: Uses Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler, Converts bytecode into native machine
  • code at runtime

questions.question: Explain Polymorphism.
questions.solution_html:
• Polymorphism means “many forms”. It allows one method or object to behave differently in
  • different situations. Types: Compile-time polymorphism (Method Overloading), Run-time
  • polymorphism (Method Overriding)
  • It improves code flexibility and reusability. Achieved using inheritance and interfaces.
  • Give an Example
  • Portable: Bytecode can be carried to any platform. Consistent behavior across systems
questions.final_answer: Portable: Bytecode can be carried to any platform. Consistent behavior across systems

  • abstract and non-abstract methods.
  • Abstract Method: A method declared without implementation. Must be implemented by

questions.question: Explain the role of javax.swing and java.applet packages in Java applications.
questions.solution_html:
• javax.swing: Used to create Graphical User Interfaces (GUI). Provides lightweight components
  • like: JButton, JFrame, JTextField
  • java.applet: Used to create applet-based applications. Applets run inside a web browser or applet
  • viewer. Extends Applet class
  • Difference: Swing → Desktop GUI applications. Applet → Browser-based applications (now
  • deprecated)
